caption: What if Earth's air vanished for just 5 seconds? Air presses on you at about 101 kPa, like the weight of 10 tonnes on every square metre, and you never feel it. Take it away and the noon sky turns black, because the blue sky is sunlight scattered by air molecules. Sound needs air to travel, so the world goes silent. Birds lose the air their wings push against. With no pressure, water boils even at room temperature, and that boiling actually cools it. In a 1965 NASA vacuum chamber accident, a test subject's last memory before passing out was the saliva on his tongue starting to boil. People stay conscious for roughly 10 seconds in a vacuum, so 5 seconds would be survivable. What would YOU notice first? 👇
